tuples.mechanism: the simultaneous fiscal, climatic, and military crisis that no single reform could answer
tuples.evidence_lens: the tax and famine relief records, the campaign reports, and the final edict

tuples.episode_object: Empress Ma, the founder's wife credited with restraining his purges
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern capital in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the consort as the only person able to moderate an autocrat, and the vacuum after her death
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals and the timing of the great purges relative to her death

tuples.episode_object: Zheng He, the admiral eunuch who commanded the treasure fleets
tuples.time_place_scope: the Indian Ocean and the East African coast in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the eunuch commander, trusted precisely because he can found no dynasty
tuples.evidence_lens: the voyage inscriptions, the shipwreck and port archaeology, and the fleet registers

tuples.episode_object: The Prince of Fu, the claimant who set up a southern court after the capital fell
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower river valleys in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the successor court that cannot agree which prince has the better claim
tuples.evidence_lens: the southern court's edicts and the competing claimants' records

tuples.episode_object: The Yongli Emperor, the last claimant, pursued into the south-western mountains
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern provinces and the Burmese border in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the fugitive court that survives on the loyalty of a single commander
tuples.evidence_lens: the correspondence of the surviving court and the pursuing campaign records

tuples.episode_object: Empress Dowager Li, the mother who ran a minority with a grand secretary
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the partnership between a dowager and a chief minister during a long minority
tuples.evidence_lens: the minister's reform records and the court's ritual documents

tuples.episode_object: Zhang Juzheng, the grand secretary who surveyed all the land and was disgraced after death
tuples.time_place_scope: the empire in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the cadastral survey and single-whip tax consolidation, and the backlash against its author
tuples.evidence_lens: the survey registers, the tax reform records, and the posthumous confiscation order

tuples.episode_object: Wei Zhongxian, the eunuch who had shrines built to himself in his own lifetime
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the provinces in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the personality cult of a palace official, and the speed of its dismantling
tuples.evidence_lens: the shrine construction records and the proscription and rehabilitation lists

tuples.episode_object: Nurhaci, the frontier chief who organised his people into banners
tuples.time_place_scope: the north-eastern forests and plains in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the banner system, which made a military organisation into a census, a tax roll, and a society
tuples.evidence_lens: the early archives in a newly created script and the banner registers

tuples.episode_object: Hong Taiji, the son who renamed a people and a dynasty before taking a capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the north-east and the Korean peninsula in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the deliberate renaming of a people and a state as an act of political construction
tuples.evidence_lens: the court archives, the Korean tributary records, and the naming edicts

tuples.episode_object: The Shunzhi Emperor, the child in whose name a regent took a capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and the capital in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the conquest carried out by a regent uncle in a child's name, and the reckoning afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the regent's edicts, the hair-cutting order, and the posthumous prosecution records

tuples.episode_object: The Kangxi Emperor, the ruler who reigned sixty-one years and could not settle his succession
tuples.time_place_scope: the empire, the steppe, and the south-western provinces in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the repeated designation and deposition of a crown prince, and the faction war it created
tuples.evidence_lens: his own vermilion rescripts, the court diaries, and the succession documents

tuples.episode_object: The Yongzheng Emperor, the son who won a disputed succession and invented a secret one
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the western frontier in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the sealed succession box, hidden behind a palace tablet and opened only at a death
tuples.evidence_lens: the palace memorial system records and the succession procedure documents

tuples.episode_object: The Qianlong Emperor, the ruler who abdicated after sixty years so as not to outdo his grandfather
tuples.time_place_scope: the empire, the western regions, and the southern tours in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the abdication for ritual reasons, followed by continued rule as a retired emperor
tuples.evidence_lens: the abdication edict, the tour accounts, and the great library compilation records

tuples.episode_object: The Jiaqing Emperor, the son who arrested his father's favourite within days
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the central provinces in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the confiscation of a favourite's fortune, which reveals the scale of a reign's corruption
tuples.evidence_lens: the confiscation inventory and the rebellion suppression records

tuples.episode_object: The Daoguang Emperor, the ruler who tried to stop an opium trade and lost a war
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern coast and the river ports in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the destruction of contraband as a policy, and the treaty system that follows a defeat
tuples.evidence_lens: the commissioner's memorials, the treaty texts, and the customs records

tuples.episode_object: The Xianfeng Emperor, the ruler who fled a capital and died at a hunting park
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital, the north-east, and the central provinces in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the simultaneous foreign war and vast internal rebellion, which together break a fiscal system
tuples.evidence_lens: the campaign records, the treaty terms, and the provincial army finance documents

tuples.episode_object: The Tongzhi Emperor, the boy under whom two dowagers governed together
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the joint regency of two empresses dowager, sitting behind a screen at audiences
tuples.evidence_lens: the regency edicts and the court audience records

tuples.episode_object: The Empress Dowager Cixi, the concubine who governed for most of five decades
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the provinces across the later nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the regency sustained by controlling which child succeeds, twice in a generation
tuples.evidence_lens: the succession edicts, the court archives, and the self-strengthening programme records

tuples.episode_object: The Guangxu Emperor, the ruler whose hundred days of reform ended in confinement
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the reform programme by edict, reversed by a palace coup within three months
tuples.evidence_lens: the reform edicts themselves and the subsequent confinement records

tuples.episode_object: Puyi, the last emperor, who abdicated at six and was used again twice
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital, the north-east, and later a prison in the twentieth century
tuples.mechanism: the abdication with favourable terms, and the later use of a deposed monarch as a foreign figurehead
tuples.evidence_lens: the abdication edict, the articles of favourable treatment, and the later state records

tuples.episode_object: Prince Gong, the brother who negotiated a peace and then ran a foreign office
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the creation of a foreign affairs office in a state that had never admitted equals
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty negotiations and the founding documents of the new office

tuples.episode_object: Dorgon, the regent uncle who ruled in all but name and was condemned after death
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and the capital in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the regent's posthumous prosecution, which lets a court disown its own conquest policies
tuples.evidence_lens: the regency edicts and the posthumous stripping of titles

tuples.episode_object: Empress Dowager Ci'an, the senior dowager whose quiet authority is hard to trace
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the co-regent whose influence is real and almost invisible in the official record
tuples.evidence_lens: the joint edicts and the court's protocol records

tuples.episode_object: Yinreng, the crown prince named twice and deposed twice
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the designated heir whose long designation makes him the target of every other prince
tuples.evidence_lens: the deposition edicts and the court's investigation records

tuples.episode_object: Prince Chun, the father of an emperor who had to refuse every honour offered him
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the awkward position of a living father of an adopted emperor, resolved by ostentatious refusal
tuples.evidence_lens: his petitions declining honours and the court's rulings

tuples.episode_object: Heshen, the guard officer who became the richest official in the empire
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the favourite whose fortune is built from the tribute and procurement system he administers
tuples.evidence_lens: the confiscation inventory and the memorials against him

tuples.episode_object: The Xuantong regency, the council that ran an empire for three years and then signed it away
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the twentieth century
tuples.mechanism: the regency that negotiates its own dissolution in exchange for a pension and a palace
tuples.evidence_lens: the abdication documents and the terms of the settlement

tuples.episode_object: Empress Suiko, the first reigning empress, who governed with a powerful regent nephew
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yamato plain in the sixth and seventh centuries
tuples.mechanism: the reigning empress paired with a regent, an arrangement that recurs for centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: the eighth-century court chronicles and the temple foundation records

tuples.episode_object: Emperor Tenmu, the ruler who won a succession war and commissioned a national history
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yamato plain in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the commissioning of an official history to establish a dynasty's descent from the gods
tuples.evidence_lens: the two surviving court chronicles and the law code fragments

tuples.episode_object: Empress Genmei, the ruler who moved a capital to a permanent grid city
tuples.time_place_scope: the Nara basin in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the permanent capital, replacing the practice of moving a court on each ruler's death
tuples.evidence_lens: the city plan, the wooden document strips, and the chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Emperor Kanmu, the ruler who moved the capital again to escape a temple establishment
tuples.time_place_scope: the Kyoto basin in the eighth and ninth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the relocation undertaken to break the political weight of a monastic establishment
tuples.evidence_lens: the construction records and the temple land registers

tuples.episode_object: Fujiwara no Michinaga, the regent who married four daughters to four emperors
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the tenth and eleventh centuries
tuples.mechanism: the maternal regency system, in which a grandfather governs through an infant emperor
tuples.evidence_lens: his own diary, the court diaries of rivals, and the marriage records

tuples.episode_object: Emperor Shirakawa, the ruler who abdicated and governed for forty years from retirement
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the eleventh and twelfth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the cloistered rule, in which a retired emperor governs free of ceremonial constraint
tuples.evidence_lens: the retired emperor's office records and contemporary diaries

tuples.episode_object: Emperor Go-Shirakawa, the retired sovereign who survived two wars by changing sides
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the twelfth century
tuples.mechanism: the survival of a ceremonial authority by conferring legitimacy on whichever warrior wins
tuples.evidence_lens: the war tales, the court diaries, and the edicts of appointment

tuples.episode_object: Minamoto no Yoritomo, the exile who built a military government in a coastal town
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern plain and a coastal valley in the twelfth century
tuples.mechanism: the parallel warrior government, which governs land and vassals while a court keeps the titles
tuples.evidence_lens: the shogunate's own chronicle and the land steward appointment records

tuples.episode_object: Hojo Masako, the widow who ran a warrior government as a nun
tuples.time_place_scope: the coastal capital in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the regency of a founder's widow, exercised through her natal family's control of the office
tuples.evidence_lens: the shogunate chronicle and the regency appointment records

tuples.episode_object: Emperor Go-Daigo, the sovereign who overthrew a military government and lost the next one
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital, an island exile, and the southern mountains in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the imperial restoration that fails because it cannot reward the warriors who won it
tuples.evidence_lens: the restoration edicts, the war tales, and the rival courts' documents

tuples.episode_object: Ashikaga Takauji, the general who changed sides twice and founded a shogunate
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the western provinces in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the two rival imperial courts, each legitimating a different warrior alliance
tuples.evidence_lens: the two courts' edicts and the shogunate's founding documents

tuples.episode_object: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, the shogun who accepted a foreign title to open a trade
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the East China Sea in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the tally trade, in which accepting a tributary status buys a licensed and profitable commerce
tuples.evidence_lens: the tally certificates and the diplomatic correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Ashikaga Yoshimasa, the shogun who built a silver pavilion while a capital burned
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the succession dispute inside a shogunal house that ignites a decade-long war in the capital
tuples.evidence_lens: the war chronicles, the temple records, and the surviving villa

tuples.episode_object: Oda Nobunaga, the lord who unified half a country and was killed by his own officer
tuples.time_place_scope: the central provinces in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the use of massed firearms and castle towns to break a coalition of temples and lords
tuples.evidence_lens: a foreign missionary's account, the castle archaeology, and the vassal records

tuples.episode_object: Toyotomi Hideyoshi, the peasant soldier who ended a civil war and invaded a peninsula
tuples.time_place_scope: the central provinces and Korea in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the sword hunt and land survey, which fixed a class boundary and a tax base at the same time
tuples.evidence_lens: the survey registers, the sword hunt edict, and the Korean campaign records

tuples.episode_object: Tokugawa Ieyasu, the patient lord who won a decisive battle at fifty-seven
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern plain and a central battlefield at the turn of the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the alternate attendance system, which held lords in place by making them keep two households
tuples.evidence_lens: the house laws, the attendance records, and the domain assessments

tuples.episode_object: Tokugawa Iemitsu, the shogun who closed a country to most foreign trade
tuples.time_place_scope: the archipelago and a southern port in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the restriction of foreign contact to a single supervised island, for religious and fiscal control
tuples.evidence_lens: the successive edicts and the trading post's own records

tuples.episode_object: Tokugawa Yoshimune, the shogun who cut costs and put a complaints box outside a gate
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern capital in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the reform of a shogunal budget by sumptuary law and by taxing domains directly
tuples.evidence_lens: the reform ordinances and the rice price records

tuples.episode_object: Tokugawa Yoshinobu, the last shogun, who resigned an office rather than fight for it
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the eastern capital in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the voluntary surrender of an office in the hope of retaining influence within a new order
tuples.evidence_lens: the resignation memorial and the restoration decree

tuples.episode_object: Emperor Meiji, the young sovereign in whose name a warrior order was dismantled
tuples.time_place_scope: the old capital and the new eastern capital in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the return of domain registers to the throne, which abolished a feudal order by paperwork
tuples.evidence_lens: the charter oath, the domain abolition decrees, and the pension settlements

coverage_profiles.subject: Korean kings of Goryeo and Joseon

tuples.episode_object: Taejo of Goryeo, the merchant's son who unified a peninsula by marrying twenty-nine times
tuples.time_place_scope: the central peninsula in the tenth century
tuples.mechanism: the marriage alliance with every regional power, which unifies a country and complicates a succession
tuples.evidence_lens: the dynastic history, his ten injunctions, and the regional clan records

tuples.episode_object: Gwangjong, the king who freed slaves and introduced an examination system
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula in the tenth century
tuples.mechanism: the civil examination adopted from a neighbour to build officials who owe the throne everything
tuples.evidence_lens: the examination records and the slave status review decrees

tuples.episode_object: Seongjong of Goryeo, the ruler who reorganised a state on a neighbour's administrative model
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula in the tenth century
tuples.mechanism: the deliberate importation of a foreign bureaucratic template, and the local adaptations it needs
tuples.evidence_lens: the memorials proposing the reforms and the resulting statutes

tuples.episode_object: Hyeonjong, the king who fled two invasions and commissioned a printed canon in response
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and the northern frontier in the eleventh century
tuples.mechanism: the vow-project, in which an enormous religious printing programme is undertaken as a defence measure
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving woodblock records and the campaign chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Injong, the king caught between a rebel monk and a court faction over moving a capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula in the twelfth century
tuples.mechanism: the geomantic argument for relocating a capital, used as cover for a factional struggle
tuples.evidence_lens: the dynastic history's account and the rebellion records

tuples.episode_object: Uijong, the king deposed by his own military officers
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the coast in the twelfth century
tuples.mechanism: the military coup provoked by the systematic humiliation of officers by civil officials
tuples.evidence_lens: the dynastic history and the subsequent military regime's records

tuples.episode_object: Choe Chungheon, the general who founded a family dictatorship lasting sixty years
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the hereditary military dictatorship that keeps kings on the throne as legitimating figures
tuples.evidence_lens: the private household office records and the dynastic history

tuples.episode_object: Gojong of Goryeo, the king who moved his court to an island for thirty years
tuples.time_place_scope: a western island and the mainland in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the island refuge, which preserves a court from cavalry while the countryside is devastated
tuples.evidence_lens: the island fortifications, the campaign records, and the second printed canon

tuples.episode_object: Gongmin, the king who threw off a steppe overlordship and lost his queen
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the reform programme that reverses a century of foreign marriage and appointment control
tuples.evidence_lens: the reform edicts and the diplomatic records with the declining overlord

tuples.episode_object: Taejo of Joseon, the general who turned an army around at an island and founded a dynasty
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern frontier and a new capital in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the commander who refuses an ordered campaign, returns, and takes the state
tuples.evidence_lens: the dynastic annals and the new capital's construction records

tuples.episode_object: Taejong of Joseon, the son who killed his brothers and built a strong central state
tuples.time_place_scope: the new capital in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the reduction of private armies to a single royal one, carried out by a prince who had used one
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals and the military reorganisation statutes

tuples.episode_object: Sejong the Great, the king who commissioned an alphabet for people who could not read
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and the northern frontier in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the design of a phonetic script by a state project, and the scholarly resistance to it
tuples.evidence_lens: the promulgation document explaining the design and the objecting memorials

tuples.episode_object: Sejo, the uncle who took a nephew's throne and killed the officials who objected
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the usurpation followed by a legal code, which converts a coup into an administrative legacy
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals and the great code compiled in his reign

tuples.episode_object: Yeonsangun, the king deposed for purges and never given a temple name
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the deposition that erases a ruler from the ritual record while keeping the annals
tuples.evidence_lens: the deposition records and the annals kept under a demoted title

tuples.episode_object: Seonjo, the king who fled a capital during an invasion and relied on a navy
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and its southern seas in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the naval interdiction of an invader's supply line, which decides a land war at sea
tuples.evidence_lens: the admiral's war diary, the court annals, and the campaign correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Gwanghaegun, the king who balanced two rival powers and was deposed for it
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and the northern frontier in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the neutral policy between a declining and a rising power, unacceptable to an ideological court
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals and the deposition manifesto

tuples.episode_object: Injo, the king who submitted at a river fort after a winter siege
tuples.time_place_scope: a fortress south of the capital in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the ritual submission ceremony, which converts a military defeat into a permanent tributary status
tuples.evidence_lens: the surrender monument and the annals of the siege

tuples.episode_object: Yeongjo, the king who reigned fifty-two years and had his son shut in a rice chest
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the elimination of an heir by a father, and the factional politics that surrounded the act
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals, the widow's memoir, and the later rehabilitation records

tuples.episode_object: Jeongjo, the grandson who built a fortress city and tried to break the factions
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital and a new walled city in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the construction of a planned city as a political base outside a capital's faction networks
tuples.evidence_lens: the illustrated construction record and the royal library's documents

tuples.episode_object: Queen Munjeong, the dowager who governed for her son and reversed a religious policy
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the dowager regency used to restore a suppressed religion's institutions for a generation
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals and the temple restoration records

tuples.episode_object: Babur, the displaced prince who lost a homeland twice and won a subcontinent's north
tuples.time_place_scope: Central Asia, Kabul, and the northern Indian plain in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the dispossessed prince who converts a failed homeland claim into a conquest elsewhere
tuples.evidence_lens: his own frank memoir and the campaign records

tuples.episode_object: Humayun, the emperor who lost an empire, spent fifteen years in exile, and won it back
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain, Sind, and Persia in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the exile restored by a foreign monarch's troops, and the cultural debt that follows
tuples.evidence_lens: a sister's memoir, the Persian court records, and the campaign accounts

tuples.episode_object: Sher Shah Suri, the interloper who governed so well his roads and coins outlasted him
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and the eastern provinces in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the trunk road, the standard silver coin, and the land survey adopted by his own supplanters
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving road and rest houses, the coinage, and the revenue records

tuples.episode_object: Akbar, the emperor who could not read and built the most literate court of his age
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and a purpose-built capital in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the ranked officer system, which converted nobles into salaried officers with defined obligations
tuples.evidence_lens: the great administrative gazetteer, the debate hall records, and the revenue registers

tuples.episode_object: Jahangir, the emperor who kept a diary and delegated much of the government to his wife
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and Kashmir in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the empress issuing coins and orders in her own name, an arrangement recorded without embarrassment
tuples.evidence_lens: his own memoirs, the coins bearing her name, and the ambassadors' reports

tuples.episode_object: Nur Jahan, the widow who married an emperor and effectively ran a state
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the consort's junta of relatives, which becomes the government and then the succession problem
tuples.evidence_lens: the coinage, the imperial orders bearing her seal, and the court histories

tuples.episode_object: Shah Jahan, the emperor who built a tomb, a capital, and a throne of jewels
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain, the Deccan, and Central Asia in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the monumental building programme as fiscal policy, absorbing a surplus and employing an economy
tuples.evidence_lens: the building accounts, the court chronicle, and the surviving monuments

tuples.episode_object: Aurangzeb, the son who imprisoned his father and spent decades campaigning in the south
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and the Deccan plateau in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the endless southern war, which consumes a treasury and hollows out a northern administration
tuples.evidence_lens: the campaign records, the revenue documents, and the legal compilation made in his reign

tuples.episode_object: Dara Shikoh, the heir who translated scriptures and lost a war of succession
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the succession war among brothers, in which the best-placed candidate is not the best general
tuples.evidence_lens: his translations, the battle accounts, and the trial record

tuples.episode_object: Jahandar Shah, the emperor made and unmade by a nobleman's faction within a year
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the kingmaker noble, whose control of a treasury decides which prince wins a succession
tuples.evidence_lens: the court chronicles and the succession campaign records

tuples.episode_object: Farrukhsiyar, the emperor who granted a trading company a customs exemption
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and the Bengal coast in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the grant of duty-free trade, which converts a commercial concession into a political foothold
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving grant document and the company's own records

tuples.episode_object: Muhammad Shah, the emperor who watched an invader carry off a jewelled throne
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the raid that removes a treasury and with it a state's ability to pay its own army
tuples.evidence_lens: the invasion accounts and the subsequent revenue collapse figures

tuples.episode_object: Shah Alam the Second, the emperor who signed away a province's revenue collection
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and the eastern provinces in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the grant of revenue collection rights to a company, which separates tax from government
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty document and the company's revenue accounts

tuples.episode_object: Bahadur Shah the Second, the last emperor, a poet tried and exiled after a rebellion
tuples.time_place_scope: the old capital and Burma in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the aged figurehead adopted by a rebellion he did not start and could not direct
tuples.evidence_lens: the trial record, his surviving verse, and the exile correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Gulbadan Begum, the princess who was asked to write down what she remembered
tuples.time_place_scope: Kabul and the northern plain in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the commissioned family memoir, written by a woman inside a household nobody else could describe
tuples.evidence_lens: her own surviving manuscript

tuples.episode_object: Jahanara Begum, the princess who chose her imprisoned father over her victorious brother
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the imperial princess with her own revenue and ships, and the political cost of loyalty
tuples.evidence_lens: her endowment records, ship ownership documents, and the court chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Murad Bakhsh, the brother who declared himself emperor and was executed for an old murder charge
tuples.time_place_scope: the western provinces in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the legal pretext used to remove a defeated brother without making him a martyr
tuples.evidence_lens: the trial record and the succession war accounts

tuples.episode_object: Akbar the Second, the pensioned emperor who sent an envoy to a foreign parliament
tuples.time_place_scope: the old capital and London in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the pensioned sovereign whose only remaining instrument is a petition to a distant legislature
tuples.evidence_lens: the envoy's own writings and the company's correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Zeb-un-Nissa, the poet princess confined for two decades
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the confinement of a royal woman for suspected correspondence with a rebel brother
tuples.evidence_lens: the attributed poetry collection and the court chronicle notices

tuples.episode_object: Kam Bakhsh, the youngest son who was told to divide an empire and fought instead
tuples.time_place_scope: the Deccan plateau in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the partition instruction in a will, which no son has ever been known to honour
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving testamentary letters and the campaign records

tuples.episode_object: Chandragupta Maurya, the young man who took a throne and traded a frontier for elephants
tuples.time_place_scope: the Gangetic plain and the north-western passes in the fourth century before our era
tuples.mechanism: the frontier treaty exchanging territory for war elephants, recorded by both sides
tuples.evidence_lens: a Greek ambassador's fragments and later Indian sources

tuples.episode_object: Bindusara, the successor who kept an empire and asked a foreign king for a philosopher
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain and the Deccan in the third century before our era
tuples.mechanism: the diplomatic gift request, which shows a court's sense of what a peer relationship involved
tuples.evidence_lens: fragments of Greek diplomatic reports and later traditions

tuples.episode_object: Ashoka, the emperor who carved his change of policy onto rocks across a subcontinent
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain, the Deccan, and the eastern coast in the third century before our era
tuples.mechanism: the published edict programme, addressed to subjects in local scripts and languages
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving rock and pillar edicts and their multiple scripts

tuples.episode_object: Dasharatha, the grandson whose short reign is known from cave dedications
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern hills in the third century before our era
tuples.mechanism: the cave grant to an ascetic order, which is sometimes the only record a reign leaves
tuples.evidence_lens: the dedicatory inscriptions in rock-cut caves

tuples.episode_object: Pushyamitra Shunga, the general who ended a dynasty at a military review
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain in the second century before our era
tuples.mechanism: the coup at a parade, and the religious realignment a new dynasty advertises
tuples.evidence_lens: later literary accounts and the sculptural programmes of the period

tuples.episode_object: Chandragupta the First, the Gupta founder who married into an older ruling house
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Ganges valley in the fourth century
tuples.mechanism: the marriage into a prestigious lineage, advertised on coins showing both spouses
tuples.evidence_lens: the joint coin issues and the later dynastic inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: Samudragupta, the ruler whose campaigns are listed on a pillar already centuries old
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain, the eastern coast, and the Deccan in the fourth century
tuples.mechanism: the reuse of an older monument to inscribe a new dynasty's claims onto an ancient authority
tuples.evidence_lens: the pillar inscription itself and the gold coin types

tuples.episode_object: Chandragupta the Second, the ruler under whom a foreign monk travelled and wrote it down
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain and the western coast in the fourth and fifth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the outsider's travel account as evidence for ordinary administration a court never recorded
tuples.evidence_lens: the pilgrim's travel record and the cave inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: Kumaragupta, the ruler who endowed a monastic university
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern plain in the fifth century
tuples.mechanism: the endowed teaching institution, funded by villages assigned to it in perpetuity
tuples.evidence_lens: the land grant plates and the excavated monastic complex

tuples.episode_object: Skandagupta, the ruler who repaired a dam and repelled a steppe invasion
tuples.time_place_scope: the western plateau and the northern frontier in the fifth century
tuples.mechanism: the public works inscription, which records a repair as an act of government
tuples.evidence_lens: a rock inscription describing the dam repair and the coin debasement record

tuples.episode_object: Harsha, the ruler who convened great assemblies and gave away his treasury at them
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the periodic distribution assembly, which converts a treasury into loyalty and religious merit
tuples.evidence_lens: a court poet's biography and a foreign pilgrim's detailed account

tuples.episode_object: Vijayalaya, the chieftain who took a town and founded a long southern dynasty
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern river delta in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the small conquest that becomes a dynasty because it controls an irrigated delta's revenue
tuples.evidence_lens: the temple inscriptions and the later dynastic genealogies

tuples.episode_object: Rajaraja the First, the ruler who built a great temple and audited its accounts on its walls
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern delta and the sea routes in the tenth and eleventh centuries
tuples.mechanism: the temple as a treasury, employer, and archive, with its accounts carved where all could see
tuples.evidence_lens: the temple's own inscribed accounts and the naval expedition records

tuples.episode_object: Rajendra the First, the ruler who sent a fleet across a sea and dug a great tank
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern delta, the Ganges, and South-East Asia in the eleventh century
tuples.mechanism: the maritime expedition against trading rivals, and the irrigation work funded by it
tuples.evidence_lens: the campaign inscriptions and the surviving reservoir

tuples.episode_object: Kulottunga the First, the ruler who abolished tolls and left a nickname for it
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern delta and the eastern coast in the eleventh and twelfth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the abolition of internal tolls, advertised as a policy and remembered as an epithet
tuples.evidence_lens: the inscriptions recording the abolition and merchant guild records

tuples.episode_object: Rajadhiraja, the ruler killed on an elephant in a battle his brother then won
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern plateau in the eleventh century
tuples.mechanism: the battlefield succession, in which a brother is crowned on the field to hold an army together
tuples.evidence_lens: the campaign inscriptions and the temple records of the coronation

tuples.episode_object: Sanghamitta, the princess sent abroad with a sapling and an order
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern coast and an island to the south in the third century before our era
tuples.mechanism: the religious mission as diplomacy, sending a royal family member to establish an order abroad
tuples.evidence_lens: island chronicles and the tree cult's continuous records

tuples.episode_object: Prabhavatigupta, the princess who governed a neighbouring kingdom as a widow regent
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Deccan in the fourth and fifth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the daughter married into a neighbouring dynasty who then governs it for her sons
tuples.evidence_lens: her own copper plate grants naming her natal dynasty

tuples.episode_object: Chanakya, the adviser whose treatise reads like an audit manual
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain in the fourth and third centuries before our era
tuples.mechanism: the administrative treatise on spies, prices, and land, whose date and authorship are argued over
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving treatise and the scholarly debate about its layers

tuples.episode_object: Rajendra the Second, the ruler who kept a merchant guild and a royal fleet working as one
tuples.time_place_scope: the Bay of Bengal and the Malay coast in the eleventh century
tuples.mechanism: the merchant guild and royal fleet partnership, which made an expedition commercially rational
tuples.evidence_lens: the guild inscriptions and the overseas campaign records

tuples.episode_object: Jayavarman the Second, the ruler whose mountain ceremony founded a kingdom's idea of itself
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern hills above a great lake in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the consecration rite declaring a universal monarch, which founded a dynastic ideology
tuples.evidence_lens: a much later foundation stele and the archaeology of the early capitals

tuples.episode_object: Yasovarman the First, the king who built a capital around a reservoir
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain north of the great lake in the ninth and tenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the great reservoir as the centre of a capital, combining water control, ritual, and display
tuples.evidence_lens: the foundation inscriptions, the hydraulic archaeology, and the temple mountain

tuples.episode_object: Suryavarman the Second, the king who built the greatest temple and campaigned east
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain and the eastern coast in the twelfth century
tuples.mechanism: the temple as a funerary monument and an astronomical instrument at the same time
tuples.evidence_lens: the temple's own reliefs and inscriptions, and the campaign records of neighbours

tuples.episode_object: Jayavarman the Seventh, the king who built hospitals and rest houses along his roads
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain and the roads to the frontiers in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the road network with hospitals and rest houses, recorded on standard inscribed stelae
tuples.evidence_lens: the hospital stelae, the road archaeology, and the surviving temple faces

tuples.episode_object: Indravarman the First, the king who dug the first great reservoir and built for his ancestors
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the ancestor temple, in which a new king anchors his legitimacy in constructed genealogy
tuples.evidence_lens: the foundation inscriptions and the temple's dedication texts

tuples.episode_object: Ramkhamhaeng, the king credited with a script and an inscription whose date is argued about
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper central plain in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the founding inscription whose authenticity is itself a long-running scholarly dispute
tuples.evidence_lens: the stone inscription and the scholarly debate over its language and date

tuples.episode_object: Trailok, the king who wrote down a ranked social order in numbers
tuples.time_place_scope: the central plain in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the dignity-mark system, assigning every subject a number that fixed land, rank, and obligation
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving law compilations and the administrative palace law

tuples.episode_object: Naresuan, the prince held hostage abroad who came home and won a war of independence
tuples.time_place_scope: the central plain and the western hills in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the royal hostage returned, who converts a childhood in an enemy court into strategic knowledge
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles of two kingdoms and the campaign sites

tuples.episode_object: Narai, the king who exchanged embassies with a distant western court
tuples.time_place_scope: the central plain and a river port in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the foreign favourite at court, and the violent reaction when his patron's health fails
tuples.evidence_lens: the embassy accounts from both sides and the revolution records

tuples.episode_object: Taksin, the general who rebuilt a kingdom in fifteen years and was deposed at the end
tuples.time_place_scope: the central plain and a new river capital in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the reconstruction of a state after a capital's destruction, and the strain it puts on its builder
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles, the campaign records, and the succession documents

tuples.episode_object: Rama the First, the general who founded a dynasty and rebuilt a legal code from memory
tuples.time_place_scope: a new capital on a river bend in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the recompilation of a destroyed law code from surviving fragments and recollection
tuples.evidence_lens: the three-seal law code and the capital's foundation records

tuples.episode_object: Mongkut, the king who spent twenty-seven years as a monk before reigning
tuples.time_place_scope: the central plain and the treaty ports in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the treaty concessions granted to avoid colonisation, and the reform programme funded by trade
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty texts, his own correspondence, and the astronomical observation records

tuples.episode_object: Chulalongkorn, the king who abolished a form of servitude gradually over a generation
tuples.time_place_scope: the kingdom and its frontiers in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the phased abolition designed so that no cohort is freed into destitution
tuples.evidence_lens: the successive decrees and the administrative reform records

tuples.episode_object: Anawrahta, the king who unified a valley and imported a canon of scripture
tuples.time_place_scope: the dry zone of a great river valley in the eleventh century
tuples.mechanism: the conquest undertaken to acquire relics and texts, which then reorganises a kingdom's religion
tuples.evidence_lens: the temple inscriptions and the irrigation works of the dry zone

tuples.episode_object: Kyansittha, the king who built a great temple and left inscriptions in four languages
tuples.time_place_scope: the river valley in the eleventh and twelfth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the multilingual inscription, addressing several populations inside one kingdom
tuples.evidence_lens: the four-language inscription and the temple's own dedicatory texts

tuples.episode_object: Bayinnaung, the king who conquered neighbours and left them their own kings
tuples.time_place_scope: the river valley and the neighbouring plains in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the tributary overlordship that leaves local dynasties in place and collects manpower instead
tuples.evidence_lens: the bell inscriptions, the chronicles, and the neighbouring kingdoms' records

tuples.episode_object: Alaungpaya, the village headman who founded a dynasty in eight years
tuples.time_place_scope: the dry zone and the southern delta in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the rapid rise of a local leader during a collapse, held together by personal loyalty alone
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles and the foreign trading posts' correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Bodawpaya, the king who ordered a census and an unfinished pagoda
tuples.time_place_scope: the river valley in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the revenue inquest, a household-by-household survey that survives as an administrative archive
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving inquest registers and the unfinished monument

tuples.episode_object: Mindon, the king who founded a new capital and had a canon carved on stone slabs
tuples.time_place_scope: the dry zone in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the durable publication project, carving a scriptural canon in stone against future loss
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving stone library and the reform administration's records

tuples.episode_object: Thibaw, the last king, exiled with his queen to a coastal town abroad
tuples.time_place_scope: the river valley and the western Indian coast in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the annexation triggered by a commercial dispute and a diplomatic ultimatum
tuples.evidence_lens: the ultimatum documents, the trading company records, and the exile accounts

coverage_profiles.subject: the early caliphs and the Umayyads

tuples.episode_object: Abu Bakr, the first successor, who spent his short rule holding a coalition together
tuples.time_place_scope: the Arabian peninsula in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the succession by consultation among leading companions, and the immediate secessions it faced
tuples.evidence_lens: later historical compilations and the earliest documentary fragments

tuples.episode_object: Umar, the caliph who organised a conquest into provinces and a stipend register
tuples.time_place_scope: Arabia, Syria, Iraq, and Egypt in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the register of stipends, which paid warriors by seniority and fixed a social hierarchy
tuples.evidence_lens: the administrative traditions preserved in later histories and early papyri

tuples.episode_object: Uthman, the caliph who standardised a text and was killed by provincial soldiers
tuples.time_place_scope: the Arabian peninsula, Egypt, and Iraq in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the standardisation of a scriptural text and the provincial grievances over appointments
tuples.evidence_lens: early manuscript evidence and the historical accounts of the revolt

tuples.episode_object: Ali, the caliph whose rule was contested from the first day to the last
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq, Syria, and Arabia in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the arbitration agreement that splits a party and creates a third faction
tuples.evidence_lens: the accounts of the arbitration and the collections of sermons attributed to him

tuples.episode_object: Muawiya, the governor who became caliph and made the office hereditary
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria and the Mediterranean coast in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the transformation of an elective office into a dynastic one by nominating a son in advance
tuples.evidence_lens: Syrian administrative papyri, coin issues, and later hostile histories

tuples.episode_object: Yazid the First, the son whose succession was resisted and whose reign ended in sieges
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria, Iraq, and Arabia in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the contested hereditary succession, and the events that became a permanent confessional memory
tuples.evidence_lens: the historical narratives of both traditions and the coin record

tuples.episode_object: Abd al-Malik, the caliph who minted a new coinage and built a domed shrine
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria, Iraq, and Jerusalem in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the currency and language reform, which replaced imperial models with a new administrative idiom
tuples.evidence_lens: the reformed coins, the shrine's dated inscription, and the administrative papyri

tuples.episode_object: Al-Walid the First, the caliph who built great mosques and pushed two frontiers at once
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria, Spain, and Central Asia in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the simultaneous expansion east and west, financed by a newly efficient tax administration
tuples.evidence_lens: the mosque inscriptions, the conquest narratives, and the provincial tax papyri

tuples.episode_object: Umar the Second, the caliph who tried to end the tax advantage of one group over another
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria and the provinces in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the fiscal reform that removes a conversion penalty and thereby threatens a revenue base
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving fiscal rescript and the provincial administrative records

tuples.episode_object: Hisham, the caliph who governed carefully for two decades while the ground shifted
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria, North Africa, and Central Asia in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the long administrative reign whose revolts are contained rather than resolved
tuples.evidence_lens: the desert palaces, the campaign records, and the provincial correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Marwan the Second, the last of the line, defeated at a river and hunted into Egypt
tuples.time_place_scope: the Jazira, Iraq, and Egypt in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the revolutionary movement organised in a distant province by missionaries before any army marches
tuples.evidence_lens: the movement's own later accounts and the campaign records

tuples.episode_object: Abd al-Rahman the First, the survivor who escaped west and founded a rival state
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria, North Africa, and the Iberian peninsula in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the fugitive prince who founds a successor state on the strength of client loyalties abroad
tuples.evidence_lens: the Andalusi chronicles and the mosque's foundation phases

tuples.episode_object: Al-Hajjaj, the governor whose severity is the most reported thing about a whole period
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and the eastern provinces in the seventh and eighth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the provincial governor as the sharp end of a caliphate, and the historiography that concentrates blame on him
tuples.evidence_lens: the administrative measures attributed to him and the hostile later histories

tuples.episode_object: Aisha bint Abi Bakr, the widow who led a party into a battle over a killing
tuples.time_place_scope: Arabia and Iraq in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the demand for justice over a predecessor's murder used as a political programme
tuples.evidence_lens: the earliest historical narratives and the traditions attributed to her

tuples.episode_object: Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson killed with his companions on a plain in Iraq
tuples.time_place_scope: Arabia and southern Iraq in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the small party marching on a promise of support that does not materialise
tuples.evidence_lens: the early historical accounts and the annual commemorative tradition

tuples.episode_object: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, the counter-caliph who held the holy cities for nine years
tuples.time_place_scope: Arabia, Iraq, and Egypt in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the rival caliphate based on the sanctuary cities, recognised across much of the empire
tuples.evidence_lens: his own coin issues and the accounts of the sieges

tuples.episode_object: Sulayman, the caliph who launched a great siege of a foreign capital and lost a fleet
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria and the Bosphorus in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the year-long siege of a fortified capital, defeated by a fleet's weapon and a winter
tuples.evidence_lens: the besieged city's chronicles and the campaign traditions

tuples.episode_object: Yazid the Third, the caliph who promised limits on his own power and reigned six months
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the accession programme promising fiscal restraint and consultation, and its brevity
tuples.evidence_lens: the accession sermon preserved in later histories

tuples.episode_object: Al-Walid the Second, the caliph remembered for verse and killed by his own family's faction
tuples.time_place_scope: Syria and the desert palaces in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the intra-dynastic coup by cousins who consider a ruler unfit for the office
tuples.evidence_lens: the poetry attributed to him and the accounts of the coup

tuples.episode_object: Musa ibn Nusayr, the governor who ordered a crossing into a peninsula and was recalled in disgrace
tuples.time_place_scope: North Africa and the Iberian peninsula in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the subordinate who conquers a province and is punished for the independence it gave him
tuples.evidence_lens: the conquest narratives and the accounts of the recall

tuples.episode_object: Al-Saffah, the first caliph of a new house, proclaimed in a provincial mosque
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and the eastern provinces in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the revolutionary movement that installs a new dynasty and then eliminates its own organisers
tuples.evidence_lens: the movement's later histories and the coin issues of the transition years

tuples.episode_object: Al-Mansur, the caliph who founded a round city and killed the man who made him
tuples.time_place_scope: the Tigris plain in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the purpose-built capital, sited for river transport and defence rather than for an existing population
tuples.evidence_lens: the city's plan as described by geographers and the administrative records

tuples.episode_object: Al-Mahdi, the caliph who spent a treasury on pilgrimage roads and postal stations
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq, Arabia, and the Anatolian frontier in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the road and postal system, which is intelligence infrastructure as much as transport
tuples.evidence_lens: the road milestones and cisterns, and the postal register descriptions

tuples.episode_object: Harun al-Rashid, the caliph whose reign is buried under the stories told about it
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq, Syria, and the Anatolian frontier in the eighth and ninth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the gap between a documented administrative reign and the legendary court of later literature
tuples.evidence_lens: the administrative and diplomatic records read against the later story collections

tuples.episode_object: The Barmakids, the vizier family who ran a state for seventeen years and fell in a night
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and the eastern provinces in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the vizieral household that becomes an alternative government, and the confiscation that ends it
tuples.evidence_lens: the confiscation records and the administrative traditions preserved in later histories

tuples.episode_object: Al-Amin, the son who lost a civil war and a capital to his own brother
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and the eastern provinces in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the divided inheritance written into a public document and repudiated by both heirs
tuples.evidence_lens: the succession document as reported and the siege accounts

tuples.episode_object: Al-Mamun, the brother who won from the east and moved the argument into theology
tuples.time_place_scope: Khurasan, Iraq, and the Anatolian frontier in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the state examination of religious scholars, which makes doctrine an administrative test
tuples.evidence_lens: the records of the inquisition and the translation movement's output

tuples.episode_object: Al-Mutasim, the caliph who bought an army of outsiders and built a city to house it
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and a new riverside capital in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the purchase and training of a slave-soldier corps loyal only to the ruler who bought them
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavated new capital and the army payroll traditions

tuples.episode_object: Al-Mutawakkil, the caliph who reversed a doctrinal policy and was killed by his own guard
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and the new capital in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the guard corps that has become the real electorate, and the anarchy that follows its first regicide
tuples.evidence_lens: the accounts of the killing and the rapid succession of the following decade

tuples.episode_object: Al-Mustain, the caliph besieged in one capital by an army holding another
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the civil war between two capitals, each holding a caliph, fought by the same army corps
tuples.evidence_lens: the siege chronicles and the coin issues from both cities

tuples.episode_object: Al-Mutadid, the caliph who partly rebuilt an administration after a long anarchy
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq in the ninth century
tuples.mechanism: the fiscal restoration after a period of military anarchy, achieved by settling arrears and revenue farms
tuples.evidence_lens: the tax farming records and the chronicles' revenue figures

tuples.episode_object: Al-Muqtadir, the caliph enthroned at thirteen and deposed twice before he was killed
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq in the tenth century
tuples.mechanism: the palace-run caliphate in which a mother and a chamberlain manage a boy's long reign
tuples.evidence_lens: the court chronicles and the vizieral turnover records

tuples.episode_object: Al-Radi, the caliph who handed his remaining powers to a commander-in-chief
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq in the tenth century
tuples.mechanism: the creation of a supreme military office that absorbs every remaining function of a ruler
tuples.evidence_lens: the appointment document and the coin and sermon protocols

tuples.episode_object: Al-Muti, the caliph who reigned entirely at the pleasure of a foreign dynasty
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq in the tenth century
tuples.mechanism: the ceremonial caliphate, kept because its endorsement legitimates the men who control it
tuples.evidence_lens: the sermon and coinage protocols and the chronicles of the controlling dynasty

tuples.episode_object: Al-Qaim, the caliph who saw one protector replaced by another in his own capital
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq in the eleventh century
tuples.mechanism: the transfer of protection from one military dynasty to another, negotiated by the protected
tuples.evidence_lens: the investiture documents and the chronicles of the entry into the capital

tuples.episode_object: Al-Nasir, the caliph who spent forty-six years rebuilding a real territorial authority
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and the eastern frontier in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the recovery of temporal power by a caliphate through guilds, diplomacy, and chivalric orders
tuples.evidence_lens: the diplomas of investiture and the chronicles of his diplomacy

tuples.episode_object: Al-Mustasim, the last caliph of the line, killed at the fall of his capital
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the siege of a capital whose defences and negotiations both fail at once
tuples.evidence_lens: the accounts of the siege from several traditions and the archaeology of the destruction

tuples.episode_object: Khayzuran, the freedwoman who became the mother of two caliphs and ran a court
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and Arabia in the eighth century
tuples.mechanism: the caliph's mother whose wealth and patronage make her a political actor in her own right
tuples.evidence_lens: the endowment records and the court chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Zubayda, the consort who funded a water supply for pilgrims across a desert
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and the Arabian pilgrimage road in the eighth and ninth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the endowed water infrastructure on a pilgrimage route, maintained for centuries afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving wells and cisterns on the route and the endowment records

tuples.episode_object: The Cairo Abbasids, the transplanted caliphs who legitimated a sultanate for two centuries
tuples.time_place_scope: Egypt in the thirteenth to sixteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the relocated caliphate, whose only function is to invest a sultan with a diploma
tuples.evidence_lens: the investiture diplomas and the sultanate's chancery manuals

tuples.episode_object: Osman, the frontier chief whose dream became a dynasty's founding story
tuples.time_place_scope: north-western Anatolia at the turn of the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the frontier raiding principality, which grows by attracting fighters rather than by administration
tuples.evidence_lens: much later chronicles read against the very thin contemporary record and coin evidence

tuples.episode_object: Orhan, the ruler who took a city, minted a coin, and married into a neighbouring empire
tuples.time_place_scope: north-western Anatolia and the straits in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the marriage into a declining empire's ruling house, which converts a raider into a legitimate ally
tuples.evidence_lens: the coin issues, the endowment deeds, and the Byzantine chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Murad the First, the sultan killed on a battlefield he had just won
tuples.time_place_scope: the Balkans and Anatolia in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the vassal system in the Balkans, which enlisted local lords rather than replacing them
tuples.evidence_lens: the vassal treaties and the battle accounts from several traditions

tuples.episode_object: Bayezid the First, the sultan captured by a conqueror from the east
tuples.time_place_scope: Anatolia and the Balkans at the turn of the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the collapse of a young state when its ruler is captured and his sons divide the remnants
tuples.evidence_lens: the battle accounts, the interregnum coinage, and the chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Mehmed the First, the son who won an eleven-year civil war between brothers
tuples.time_place_scope: Anatolia and the Balkans in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the interregnum in which several princes hold different halves and strike their own coins
tuples.evidence_lens: the parallel coin issues and the chronicles of the reunification

tuples.episode_object: Murad the Second, the sultan who abdicated for his son and was called back twice
tuples.time_place_scope: the Balkans and Anatolia in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the abdication in favour of a boy, reversed when a crusade forces an experienced commander back
tuples.evidence_lens: the campaign records and the chronicles of the two returns
