tuples.episode_object: Idia, the queen mother whose face became a court's emblem
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest belt in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the queen mother as a political office rather than a family relationship
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving ivory masks and the palace oral records

tuples.episode_object: Ovonramwen, the last independent king, exiled after a punitive expedition
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest belt and the Niger delta in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the punitive expedition following an ambush, and the removal of a court's art to foreign museums
tuples.evidence_lens: the expedition's own records, the auction catalogues, and the exile correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Dingiswayo, the chief who reorganised regiments by age rather than by clan
tuples.time_place_scope: the south-eastern grasslands in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the age-regiment, which cuts across clan loyalty and creates a standing force
tuples.evidence_lens: the oral traditions collected in the nineteenth century and the missionary accounts

tuples.episode_object: Shaka, the ruler whose reign reshaped a region in a decade
tuples.time_place_scope: the south-eastern grasslands in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the consolidation of many chiefdoms into one kingdom, and the displacement it set off
tuples.evidence_lens: the traders' eyewitness journals and the oral traditions recorded later

tuples.episode_object: Dingane, the half-brother who took a throne and lost a war on a river
tuples.time_place_scope: the south-eastern grasslands in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the treaty negotiation that ends in a killing, and the war of retribution that follows
tuples.evidence_lens: the settlers' accounts, the mission records, and the oral traditions

tuples.episode_object: Mpande, the brother who took a throne with outside help and reigned thirty years
tuples.time_place_scope: the south-eastern grasslands in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the ruler installed by a neighbouring settler republic, who then outlives its influence
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty records and the mission station correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Cetshwayo, the king who won a battle and lost a kingdom in six months
tuples.time_place_scope: the south-eastern grasslands in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the ultimatum demanding the disbandment of an army, designed to be impossible to accept
tuples.evidence_lens: the ultimatum text, the campaign records, and his own statements in exile

tuples.episode_object: Mzilikazi, the commander who broke away and founded a kingdom far to the north
tuples.time_place_scope: the interior plateau in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the secession of a regiment, which migrates and reconstitutes itself as a new kingdom
tuples.evidence_lens: the missionary journals and the oral traditions of two peoples

tuples.episode_object: Moshoeshoe the First, the chief who built a kingdom on a flat-topped mountain
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands south of the interior plateau in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the mountain stronghold plus a diplomacy of asylum, which absorbs refugees into a new nation
tuples.evidence_lens: the missionary correspondence, the treaties, and the oral traditions

tuples.episode_object: Sobhuza the First, the king who avoided two wars by moving and negotiating
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern highlands in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the strategic retreat and marriage diplomacy that preserves a small kingdom between larger ones
tuples.evidence_lens: the oral traditions and the neighbouring states' records

tuples.episode_object: Acamapichtli, the first ruler chosen from a neighbouring dynasty to give a city legitimacy
tuples.time_place_scope: the island city in a highland lake in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the borrowed dynasty, imported to give a new city a royal line with prestige
tuples.evidence_lens: the pictorial codices and the colonial-era annals compiled from them

tuples.episode_object: Huitzilihuitl, the ruler whose marriage lowered his city's tribute
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland lake basin in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the marriage into an overlord's family, which converts tribute obligations into kinship ones
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals and the tribute lists

tuples.episode_object: Chimalpopoca, the ruler killed during a war of independence from an overlord
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland lake basin in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the assassination of a compliant ruler by a faction that wants a war
tuples.evidence_lens: the several competing annals traditions of the same events

tuples.episode_object: Itzcoatl, the ruler who won independence and burned the old books
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland lake basin in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the destruction of earlier records and the writing of a new official history for a new order
tuples.evidence_lens: the later annals that report the burning and the surviving pre-conquest manuscripts

tuples.episode_object: Moctezuma the First, the ruler who built an aqueduct and a dyke against a flood
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland lake basin in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the hydraulic works that keep a saline lake out of a city's freshwater supply
tuples.evidence_lens: the archaeology of the dyke and aqueduct and the annals

tuples.episode_object: Nezahualcoyotl, the exiled prince who returned as a king and is remembered for poetry and law
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern shore of the highland lake in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the alliance of three cities, which shared tribute and war under an agreed hierarchy
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals, the legal traditions, and the surviving hillside water works

tuples.episode_object: Axayacatl, the ruler defeated by a western neighbour with better metal
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland basin and the western highlands in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the frontier that stops an expanding state, held by a rival with copper alloy weapons
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals of the campaign and the metallurgical evidence

tuples.episode_object: Tizoc, the ruler whose short reign is remembered mainly by a carved stone
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland lake basin in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the commemorative monument that outlives a reign judged unsuccessful by its own annalists
tuples.evidence_lens: the carved stone and the annals' unusual criticism

tuples.episode_object: Ahuitzotl, the ruler who expanded to two coasts and rebuilt a great temple
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands and the southern coasts in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the tribute province system, in which conquered regions send fixed goods on a fixed schedule
tuples.evidence_lens: the tribute register, the temple offerings, and the annals

tuples.episode_object: Moctezuma the Second, the ruler who reorganised a court and met a foreign expedition
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland lake basin in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the centralisation of a court that removes the older nobility, weakening a state's response to a crisis
tuples.evidence_lens: the conquerors' letters, the indigenous annals, and the later illustrated histories

tuples.episode_object: Cuitlahuac, the ruler who drove out an expedition and died of an epidemic
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland lake basin in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the epidemic that arrives with an expedition and kills a leadership faster than any battle
tuples.evidence_lens: the indigenous accounts of the sickness and the Spanish narratives

tuples.episode_object: Cuauhtemoc, the last ruler, who defended a city street by street
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland lake city in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the siege of an island city, decided by cutting an aqueduct and by boats built inland
tuples.evidence_lens: the conquerors' campaign accounts and the indigenous illustrated histories

tuples.episode_object: Pachacuti, the son who defended a city against a siege and rebuilt an empire around it
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Andes in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the reorganisation of conquest into provinces with resettled populations and a road system
tuples.evidence_lens: the colonial-era chronicles drawn from knotted cord records, and the road archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Topa Inca, the ruler who extended a road system to two more coasts
tuples.time_place_scope: the Andes and the Pacific coast in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the labour tax paid in work rather than in goods, which built roads, terraces, and storehouses
tuples.evidence_lens: the storehouse archaeology and the chronicles' descriptions of the labour system

tuples.episode_object: Huayna Capac, the ruler who died in an epidemic that arrived before any foreigner did
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Andes in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the disease that travels ahead of an expedition and removes a ruler and his heir together
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles' accounts of the sickness and the succession

tuples.episode_object: Huascar, the heir in the south who lost a civil war to his brother
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Andes in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the succession war between two sons based in two capitals with two armies
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles compiled from both sides' oral records

tuples.episode_object: Atahualpa, the victor of a civil war captured within months of winning it
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Andes in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the seizure of a ruler at a meeting, and the ransom collected before his execution
tuples.evidence_lens: the participants' own accounts and the inventories of the ransom metal

tuples.episode_object: Manco Inca, the installed ruler who rebelled and besieged his own capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Andes in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the puppet ruler who uses his position to organise a rebellion from inside
tuples.evidence_lens: the siege accounts and the later indigenous narratives

tuples.episode_object: Titu Cusi, the ruler in a mountain refuge who dictated an account of the conquest
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Andean forests in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the dictated account, in which a ruler puts his own version of events into the record
tuples.evidence_lens: his dictated narrative and the negotiation records with the colonial authorities

tuples.episode_object: Tupac Amaru, the last ruler of a mountain state, executed in a colonial square
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Andean forests and the old capital in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the elimination of a residual state and the legal justification produced afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the viceregal records, the trial documents, and the later indigenous accounts

coverage_profiles.subject: Mongol khans and the successor khanates

tuples.episode_object: Temujin, the outcast boy who became the khan of all who lived in felt tents
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern steppe in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the decimal army organisation that broke tribal units and rebuilt them around loyalty to one man
tuples.evidence_lens: a near-contemporary secret history and the later Persian and Chinese chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Ogedei, the son who built a capital and drank himself out of a campaign
tuples.time_place_scope: the central steppe and eastern Europe in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the succession assembly, which requires every senior commander to leave a campaign and ride home
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles from three traditions and the capital's archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Toregene Khatun, the widow who governed for five years and installed her son
tuples.time_place_scope: the central steppe in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the widow regency that manages an interregnum by distributing offices and gifts
tuples.evidence_lens: the Persian chronicles and a European friar's eyewitness report

tuples.episode_object: Guyuk, the khan who wrote a blunt letter to a pope
tuples.time_place_scope: the central steppe in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the demand for submission as the standard opening of a diplomatic relationship
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving letter with its seal and the friar's account of delivering it

tuples.episode_object: Sorghaghtani Beki, the princess who positioned four sons and never ruled herself
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe and northern China in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the management of appanage revenues and religious patronage to build a succession claim
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles from several traditions and the tax farming records

tuples.episode_object: Mongke, the khan who took a census of an empire and died besieging a fortress
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe, Iran, and western China in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the empire-wide census, which turned an army's spoils into a taxable administration
tuples.evidence_lens: the census records described in the chronicles and the tax registers

tuples.episode_object: Kublai, the khan who founded a Chinese dynasty and lost two fleets to storms
tuples.time_place_scope: northern China, a new capital, and the sea route to Japan in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the transformation of a steppe khanate into a settled dynasty with a Chinese administration
tuples.evidence_lens: the dynastic history, a foreign merchant's travel account, and the wreck archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Ariq Boke, the brother who was elected in the homeland and lost the war for it
tuples.time_place_scope: the central steppe and northern China in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the split between a steppe-based and a settled-based claimant, which ends a single empire
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles from both sides and the coinage of the rival courts

tuples.episode_object: Jochi, the eldest son whose paternity was questioned and whose descendants ruled the west
tuples.time_place_scope: the western steppe in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the disputed paternity that redirects an inheritance to the far end of an empire
tuples.evidence_lens: the secret history's account and the later western chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Chagatai, the second son who kept the old law and got the middle lands
tuples.time_place_scope: Central Asia in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the appanage in the middle of an empire, which becomes the most conservative of the successor states
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles and the coinage of the Central Asian towns

tuples.episode_object: Batu, the commander who reached the Adriatic and turned back
tuples.time_place_scope: the western steppe, Rus, and central Europe in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the campaign broken off by a succession assembly rather than by any defeat
tuples.evidence_lens: the European chronicles, the Rus chronicles, and the Persian histories

tuples.episode_object: Berke, the khan who allied with a distant sultanate against his own cousins
tuples.time_place_scope: the western steppe and the Caucasus in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the alliance across a religious line against kin, which fixes a permanent split in a family empire
tuples.evidence_lens: the diplomatic correspondence and the Mamluk chancery records

tuples.episode_object: Hulegu, the brother who took two capitals and founded a Persian khanate
tuples.time_place_scope: Iran, Iraq, and the Levant in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the siege train of engineers moved thousands of miles to reduce fortified cities
tuples.evidence_lens: the Persian chronicles, the Armenian accounts, and the observatory he endowed

tuples.episode_object: Ghazan, the khan who converted, reformed the taxes, and rebuilt the coinage
tuples.time_place_scope: Iran and Iraq at the turn of the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the tax reform that ends arbitrary requisition by fixing rates and abolishing relay abuses
tuples.evidence_lens: his chief minister's own history and the reform edicts it preserves

tuples.episode_object: Nogai, the commander who made khans for twenty years without becoming one
tuples.time_place_scope: the western steppe and the Danube in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the general who prefers to appoint khans rather than to be one, until a client turns on him
tuples.evidence_lens: the Byzantine, Rus, and Mamluk accounts of his interventions

tuples.episode_object: Toqta, the khan who destroyed his kingmaker and reordered a khanate's trade
tuples.time_place_scope: the western steppe and the Black Sea ports in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the control of Black Sea trading colonies as the fiscal basis of a steppe state
tuples.evidence_lens: the Italian colonial charters and the coin issues

tuples.episode_object: Ozbeg, the khan under whom a western khanate reached its height
tuples.time_place_scope: the western steppe and the Volga in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the patents of authority issued to subordinate princes, which made a tribute system a political one
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving patents, the Rus chronicles, and the traveller accounts

tuples.episode_object: Mamai, the commander who lost a battle in the forest and then lost his khan
tuples.time_place_scope: the western steppe and the Russian forests in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the defeat of a non-royal commander, which lets a legitimate claimant sweep him aside
tuples.evidence_lens: the Rus chronicles and the coin issues of the rival claimants

tuples.episode_object: Tokhtamysh, the khan who reunited a khanate and then quarrelled with the man who made him
tuples.time_place_scope: the western steppe, Moscow, and the Caucasus in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the client who asserts independence against his patron, and the campaigns that ruin both
tuples.evidence_lens: the Persian and Rus chronicles and the destruction layers in the trading cities

tuples.episode_object: Timur, the emir who never took the title of khan and ruled through men who held it
tuples.time_place_scope: Central Asia, Iran, India, and Anatolia in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the rule exercised through a puppet khan of the right descent, because the title required it
tuples.evidence_lens: his court histories, the puppet khans' coinage, and the surviving monuments

tuples.episode_object: The false Neros, the three men who claimed to be a dead emperor within twenty years
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Mediterranean and the Parthian frontier in the first century
tuples.mechanism: the impostor sustained by a foreign power that finds a claimant useful as leverage
tuples.evidence_lens: the brief notices in several histories and the eastern diplomatic context

tuples.episode_object: Magnentius, the officer proclaimed at a birthday dinner
tuples.time_place_scope: Gaul and the Balkans in the fourth century
tuples.mechanism: the proclamation staged at a private gathering by officers who have already agreed
tuples.evidence_lens: a contemporary soldier's history and the coin issues of the usurpation

tuples.episode_object: Procopius, the relative who used a dynastic connection to raise a revolt
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern capital and Anatolia in the fourth century
tuples.mechanism: the claim advanced on kinship with a popular dead ruler rather than on any office held
tuples.evidence_lens: the narrative histories and the brief coin series

tuples.episode_object: Basiliscus, the brother-in-law who held a capital for twenty months
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern capital in the fifth century
tuples.mechanism: the usurpation that collapses when a religious policy alienates a capital's own clergy
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles and the surviving encyclical texts

tuples.episode_object: Phocas, the junior officer raised by a mutinying army on a frontier
tuples.time_place_scope: the Danube frontier and the eastern capital in the seventh century
tuples.mechanism: the mutiny over pay and winter quarters that turns into a change of dynasty
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles and the coin portraits of the new regime

tuples.episode_object: Bardas Skleros, the general who rebelled twice and negotiated a retirement
tuples.time_place_scope: Anatolia and the eastern frontier in the tenth century
tuples.mechanism: the negotiated end to a revolt, in which a rebel is pensioned rather than executed
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles and the terms of the settlement they record

tuples.episode_object: Sviatopolk, the prince whose nickname was fixed by the chronicle his rival commissioned
tuples.time_place_scope: the Rus lands in the eleventh century
tuples.mechanism: the naming of a defeated claimant by the winner's own historiography
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicle account and the later hagiographies of his brothers

tuples.episode_object: Sverre, the priest who said he was a king's son and won a twenty-year war
tuples.time_place_scope: Norway in the twelfth century
tuples.mechanism: the claim of royal descent asserted by an outsider and validated only by winning
tuples.evidence_lens: a saga written at his direction and the church's hostile correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Ivaylo, the swineherd who defeated an invasion and married an empress
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Danube in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the popular leader raised by a defence against raiders, absorbed into a dynasty by marriage
tuples.evidence_lens: the Byzantine histories and the Bulgarian chronicle notices

tuples.episode_object: The false Baldwin, the hermit who claimed to be a returned emperor
tuples.time_place_scope: Flanders and Hainaut in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the returned-ruler impostor accepted by a population with a grievance against the current one
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles of the reception and the trial records

tuples.episode_object: Owain Glyndwr, the landowner proclaimed prince who vanished rather than surrender
tuples.time_place_scope: Wales and the marches at the turn of the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the national revolt that builds a parliament and a foreign alliance before it collapses
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving correspondence, the parliamentary records, and the campaign accounts

tuples.episode_object: Edward Balliol, the claimant installed by an army of the disinherited
tuples.time_place_scope: Scotland and northern England in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the claimant sponsored by nobles seeking to recover confiscated estates rather than a crown
tuples.evidence_lens: the indentures of the disinherited and the campaign chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Jack Cade, the rebel who took a royal surname and held a capital for days
tuples.time_place_scope: the south-east of England in the fifteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the adoption of a royal family name to convert a tax revolt into a dynastic threat
tuples.evidence_lens: the rebels' own written manifesto and the trial records

tuples.episode_object: Antonio, Prior of Crato, the claimant who lost a kingdom and kept claiming from abroad
tuples.time_place_scope: Portugal, the Azores, and France in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the succession crisis decided by an invading army while the courts are still arguing
tuples.evidence_lens: the succession law arguments and the campaign records

tuples.episode_object: The four false Sebastians, the men who each claimed to be a king lost in a desert battle
tuples.time_place_scope: Portugal, Spain, and Italy in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the missing body, which supports a series of impostors for decades afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the trial records of each claimant and the popular literature of the returning king

tuples.episode_object: The first False Dmitry, the claimant who reached a throne and held it for eleven months
tuples.time_place_scope: Poland, Muscovy, and the capital at the turn of the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the impostor backed by a neighbouring nobility, who wins because the incumbent regime is unpopular
tuples.evidence_lens: the foreign envoys' accounts, the coronation records, and the later investigations

tuples.episode_object: The second False Dmitry, the claimant recognised by the first one's widow
tuples.time_place_scope: the Muscovite lands in the seventeenth century
tuples.mechanism: the second impostor validated by a witness who has every reason to validate him
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles of the period and the camp's own administrative documents

tuples.episode_object: Stephen the Little, the healer who ruled a mountain principality as a dead emperor
tuples.time_place_scope: the Adriatic mountains in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the impostor who governs competently, which is why nobody in the country wants him unmasked
tuples.evidence_lens: the Venetian and Russian diplomatic reports

tuples.episode_object: Yemelyan Pugachev, the cossack who led a rising in the name of a murdered emperor
tuples.time_place_scope: the Ural and Volga regions in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the peasant rising organised around a claim of legitimate rule, with a court and manifestos
tuples.evidence_lens: the rebels' own manifestos and the trial record

tuples.episode_object: Karl Naundorff, the clockmaker who claimed a lost dauphin's identity for thirty years
tuples.time_place_scope: Germany, France, and the Low Countries in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the identity claim pursued through courts rather than armies, in an age of documents
tuples.evidence_lens: the court filings, the police files, and the later forensic testing

tuples.episode_object: Melisende of Jerusalem, the queen who was left a co-ruler and had to fight to stay one
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine coast in the twelfth century
tuples.mechanism: the joint succession of a queen, her husband, and their son, which produces three claims
tuples.evidence_lens: the kingdom's own chronicle and the charters showing whose name appears when

tuples.episode_object: Sibylla of Jerusalem, the queen who crowned her own husband at her coronation
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine coast in the twelfth century
tuples.mechanism: the ruling queen who confers a crown on a consort of her own choosing at the ceremony itself
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles' accounts of the coronation and the succession disputes

tuples.episode_object: Tamar of Georgia, the queen crowned in her father's lifetime and titled king
tuples.time_place_scope: the Caucasus in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries
tuples.mechanism: the co-coronation during a father's life, used to pre-empt an objection to a woman's succession
tuples.evidence_lens: the royal chronicles, the church frescoes, and the coin legends

tuples.episode_object: Berenguela of Castile, the queen who inherited a kingdom and handed it to her son the same year
tuples.time_place_scope: the Iberian plateau in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the transmission of a claim through a mother who resigns it deliberately to avoid a war
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicle accounts and the charters of the transfer

tuples.episode_object: Constance of Sicily, the heiress who married an emperor and gave birth in a public tent
tuples.time_place_scope: Sicily and central Italy at the turn of the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the public birth staged to forestall any later claim that an heir was substituted
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles' accounts and the charters of her regency

tuples.episode_object: Jadwiga of Poland, the girl crowned king and married for a union
tuples.time_place_scope: Poland and Lithuania in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the crowning of a female sovereign under the male title so that her authority is unambiguous
tuples.evidence_lens: the coronation records and the union agreement's text

tuples.episode_object: Margaret, Maid of Norway, the child queen who died at sea before reaching her kingdom
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern seas and Scotland in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the succession that fails in transit, leaving a kingdom with a dozen competing claims
tuples.evidence_lens: the marriage treaty, the guardianship records, and the later competition records

tuples.episode_object: Joanna the First of Naples, the queen tried for a murder and acquitted by a pope
tuples.time_place_scope: southern Italy and Provence in the fourteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the trial of a reigning monarch before an overlord's court, and the political price of acquittal
tuples.evidence_lens: the papal trial records and the chronicles of the invasion that followed

tuples.episode_object: Bona Sforza, the foreign queen who bought estates and reorganised their rents
tuples.time_place_scope: Poland, Lithuania, and Italy in the sixteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the consort's own landholding, reorganised as a personal fiscal base independent of the crown
tuples.evidence_lens: the estate surveys, the rent rolls, and the diplomatic correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Ulrika Eleonora, the queen who accepted a throne on constitutional conditions and then abdicated
tuples.time_place_scope: Sweden in the eighteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the accession conditional on surrendering absolute power, which ends an autocracy by contract
tuples.evidence_lens: the constitutional instrument and the estates' records

tuples.episode_object: Maria the First of Portugal, the queen whose illness moved a court across an ocean
tuples.time_place_scope: Portugal and Brazil at the turn of the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the relocation of a monarchy overseas to escape an invasion, taking the archives with it
tuples.evidence_lens: the evacuation records, the fleet manifests, and the colonial administration's documents

tuples.episode_object: Maria Christina of Spain, the regent whose daughter's claim caused a civil war
tuples.time_place_scope: Spain in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the repeal of a male-only succession rule, and the armed movement it creates around the excluded uncle
tuples.evidence_lens: the pragmatic sanction, the manifestos of both sides, and the war records

tuples.episode_object: Isabella the Second of Spain, the queen who reigned from the age of three and was deposed at thirty-seven
tuples.time_place_scope: Spain and France in the nineteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the reign spent as the arbiter between generals, ending when both parties agree to remove her
tuples.evidence_lens: the ministry lists, the pronouncement records, and the abdication documents

tuples.episode_object: Razia, the sultan who dressed for public audience as her father's successor
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Indian plain in the thirteenth century
tuples.mechanism: the nomination of a daughter over sons, and the guard corps that will not accept it
tuples.evidence_lens: the contemporary Persian chronicles and the coin issues in her name

evidence_expectations: Ground each beat in the kind of record named by the slot, and describe record types rather than citing any specific title, author, or archive reference.
Prefer documentary and material evidence such as charters, chronicles, coins, inscriptions, court registers, tax rolls, wills, and surviving buildings over anecdote.
State uncertainty plainly and calmly where a date, a parentage, a cause of death, or a motive is disputed, and never resolve it with invented detail.
Say who wrote a source and when, especially where the only surviving account was produced by the winner, a successor, or a rival confession.
compatibility_rules: Pair only with the sleep history compilation formula; this pack assumes chapters of roughly even length with no shared arc, no framing device, and no narrative running between them.
Use one life per chapter and never mix two subjects inside a chapter, so that a listener waking in the middle still hears one continuous biography.
Draw the twenty slots of a subject in any order, but never reuse a slot within one compilation, since each slot is deliberately a materially different episode.
